woba_weights.comment: Update each offseason from FanGraphs 'Guts!' table for the season being modeled.

fip_constant_comment: null = auto-derive cFIP from league season totals (lgERA - lgFIP_raw). Set a number to override.

shrinkage.comment: Adds k innings / k PA of league-average performance to each single-game sample. This is the stabilizer that keeps single-game FIP positive and bounded. TUNE THIS EXPERIMENTALLY - it is the MLB analogue of the paper's experimentally-optimized pre-filter.

fip_floor_comment: Hard guard. Single-game FIP can legitimately go negative (0 HR, 0 BB, 12 K); wOBA/FIP is undefined near zero and the paper's log/sqrt/reciprocal adjustments require strictly positive input.
relative_scale_comment: Rescale strength to 100 = league mean for the season (principle 2: forecasted values must be relativistic; also moves values off the 0<x<1 domain where log10 goes negative).

prefilter.comment: As specified: drop bottom 10% and top 10% of each team's strength values. Skew before/after trimming is reported per team so you can see how much signal the trim removes.

window_comment: null = use all games this season. Set an integer (e.g. 60) to use only the most recent N games per team. The paper puts the crossover where curve-fitting beats this approximation at ~100 data points - a 162 game season exceeds that.

distribution.sigma_adj_comment: 'paper' = eq(10) sqrt(|mu_base^2 - mu_adj^2|); 'direct' = stdev of the adjusted array; 'auto' = eq(10) unless it disagrees with 'direct' by more than 5x, then fall back. See METHOD.md, open question #1.
distribution.damping_comment: 'min' = pointwise minimum of the scaled normal and scaled skew-adjusted curves. Its peak is exactly the between-peaks intersection and its shoulders are the outer intersections, reproducing the paper's mode + variance-bound construction.

prediction.home_field_comment: 0.0 = pure algorithm. MLB home teams win ~54% of games (logit ~0.16). Leave at 0 for a clean viability read, then test whether adding it improves the Brier score.
prediction.calibration_comment: 'auto' = apply the logistic recalibration in data/calibration.json when it exists (fitted by scripts/evaluate.py on completed games). Raw P(strength_A > strength_B) is over-dispersed for single MLB games - the distributions describe performance spread, not the extra run-scoring luck that decides one game. Set to 'off' to see the unrecalibrated algorithm.
